picks.style: greek tragic monody, solo aulos, low drone, ravaged male voice, very slow, unbearable, sparse
picks.why: The blinded Oedipus addressing Cithaeron, the three roads and the marriage bed — the most famous speech in Greek tragedy.

picks.style: ancient chorus hymn, lyre, frame drum, torch-lit layered voices, building, invocatory, urgent
picks.why: The prayer to the Lycean Lord's golden bowstring, Artemis' fires and Bacchus with his blazing torch — a real invocation.

picks.style: prophetic chant, deep drone, struck bell, grave old male voice, slow, implacable, gathering dread
picks.why: Teiresias: you have sight and do not see; the double lash of your parents' curse will drive you out with darkness on your eyes.

picks.style: american husking-bee tune, fiddle, banjo, hammered dulcimer, hearty male lead with mixed chorus, brisk, communal
picks.why: The husking: rustling husks, cracking cobs, laughter, and cider going round in silence — a whole night in one scene.

picks.style: mock-georgic comic air, fiddle, penny whistle, wry tenor, moderate, affectionate, jesting
picks.why: The poet recognising his cornmeal abroad by its yellow face, then blushing that Pennsylvanians call it Mush.

picks.style: mock-heroic invocation, small brass, snare, grandly ironic baritone, stately then winking, moderate
picks.why: 'Ye Alps audacious... I sing not you. A softer theme I chuse' — the joke of the whole poem stated in its opening lines.

picks.style: augustan satirical air, harpsichord, oboe, crisp cutting baritone, brisk, sardonic
picks.why: 'The greatest curses any Age has known, / Have issued from the Temple or the Throne' — with the king sucking in the sacred grease.

picks.style: patriotic declamation, martial snare, strings, ringing tenor with chorus, stirring, defiant
picks.why: 'That is Empire! shun her baleful path, / Her Words are Slavery, and her Touch is Death!' — pure singable rhetoric.

picks.style: rococo drawing-room song, fortepiano, flute, light elegant tenor, graceful, playful
picks.why: Zeuxis assembling a goddess out of borrowed features — Cynthia's brow, Lesbia's eye, Chloe's vermilion cheek.

picks.style: pastoral folk song, acoustic guitar, flute, warm tenor, gentle, wistful, with a returning refrain
picks.why: 'Ye scenes that engag'd my gay youth, / Say, whither so fast do ye fly?' — an actual song, with its question coming round again.

picks.style: english elegy ballad, harp, cello, plaintive tenor, slow, stark, catching at the turn
picks.why: The gun raised at the moving shade, and the idol of his soul falling shrieking to the ground — the ballad's whole hinge.

picks.style: deathbed lament, solo viol, low harp, tenor with a fading female voice, very slow, tender
picks.why: Her dying words forgiving the hand that killed her — 'Content beneath thy erring hand I die'.

picks.style: latin dramatic recitation with music, aulos, low strings, rising percussion, awed male voice, surging like sea swell
picks.why: The shepherd who has never seen a ship watching the Argo come on — terror, then the sailors' song heard as Silvanus' music.

picks.style: star-hymn, kithara, small bells, sustained drone, low male voice, slow, nocturnal, glittering
picks.why: The Dragon's head with its double-marked temples and two glowing eyes, gazing back at the tail of the Great Bear.

picks.style: sardonic latin chorus, low brass, plucked strings, ironic baritone with answering chorus, marching, swaggering
picks.why: 'Let me be called most base, so I be called rich' — and money outbidding mother, child and father in the face of Venus.

picks.style: roman hymn to philosophy, lyre, soft chorus, reverent tenor, slow, golden, spacious
picks.why: 'Your face is not mortal, nor does your voice sound human' — a goddess worshipped by an upright will, not slaughtered bulls.

picks.style: roman epistolary litany, solo lyre, sparse strings, half-spoken male voice, unhurried, one line at a time, reflective
picks.why: A string of quoted tags that reads as a litany — compliance gets us friends, plain speaking hate; he plants trees for a race to come.

picks.style: greek funeral epigram, bowed lyre, single low drum, unison male voices, very slow, stone-carved, solemn
picks.why: The Isthmus epitaph entire: 'When Greece upon the point of danger stood, / We fell, defending her with our life-blood.'
